answer: Bonded collateral escrows make sybil identities costly: when k coordinated identities equivocate on correlated statements, the protocol penalizes the k(k−1)/2 identity pairs, so exposure grows as O(k²), not merely with each signer. On detection, an exponential multiplier and asymmetric capital depreciation amplify swarm-wide losses, making concealed coordination riskier than honest participation. A cipher may hide links temporarily, but cannot turn the oasis of anonymity into ivory protection from verifiable evidence.
